description.comment: The golden dust stingray (Potamotrygon marinae) is a species of stingray in the family Potamotrygonidae found in rivers in tropical and subtropical South America (from Wikipedia entry). This sample of a male individual found in French Guiana, was procured by Yann Guiguen and Julien Bobe to generate genome and transcriptome data for the Vertebrate Genomes Project (VGP). Sequencing was conducted at the Vertebrate Genome Lab (VGL) at the Rockefeller University, led by Erich D. Jarvis, Giulio Formenti, and Jennifer Balacco.

assembly_info.comments: Curation note: At the time of curation, there was no reported karyotype for this species. The diploid number reported for Potamotrygon species ranges from 64 to 67/68 chromosomes (Ferreira 2023). In addition, the family Potamotrygonidae has been reported to present an X1X1X2X2 or X1X2Y sex-determination system. This sample was identified as heterogametic with X1X2Y sex chromosomes. This assembly showed duplications in centromeric regions of several chromosomes. These duplicated regions were assigned as unlocs to their respective chromosomes based on Hi-C interaction signals. In addition, shrapnel scaffolds displaying interaction signals between the Y and X1 sex chromosomes were assigned as unlocs to the Y chromosome. The numbering of the X chromosomes was assigned arbitrarily. For scaffolds placed within heterochromatic regions, neither their order nor orientation could be determined.
